overview.description: A production-ready Python bot that exploits the structural pricing lag between centralized exchange spot prices (Binance BTC/ETH WebSocket feeds) and prediction market contract odds (Polymarket CLOB short-duration UP/DOWN contracts). The bot continuously monitors Binance WebSocket streams at sub-50ms latency, detects when Polymarket contract odds diverge from the implied fair value derived from CEX price movements by more than a configurable threshold (3-5%), and executes trades against stale Polymarket pricing before the orderbook reprices. Position sizing uses fractional Kelly criterion to maximize geometric growth rate while a hard -40% drawdown kill switch prevents catastrophic loss. The system targets sub-100ms detection-to-execution latency across the full pipeline: price ingestion, divergence calculation, Kelly sizing, order construction, and CLOB submission. Based on the documented 0x8dxd wallet that turned $313 into $2.38M over 26,738 trades at 98% win rate, and validated by the Claude vs OpenClaw experiment where Kelly + kill switch produced +1,322% vs liquidation.
objectives: Maintain persistent async WebSocket connections to Binance for BTC and ETH real-time price streams with sub-50ms message receipt latency
Continuously poll or stream Polymarket CLOB orderbook state for active 5-minute and 15-minute BTC/ETH UP/DOWN contracts
Compute implied fair probability from CEX price movements using a momentum-persistence model calibrated to short-duration contract windows
Detect divergence between implied fair probability and current Polymarket contract odds exceeding configurable threshold (default: 3% for conservative, 5% for aggressive)
Size positions using fractional Kelly criterion (f* = (bp - q) / b, applied at 25-50% fraction) capped at 8% of total portfolio per single trade
Execute limit orders via Polymarket CLOB API at stale pricing within 100ms of divergence detection
Enforce hard risk limits: 0.5% max capital per trade (conservative mode), 2% daily loss limit, -40% total drawdown kill switch with immediate position flattening
Implement cost-averaging fallback: if primary arb fails, average down with entries below 35 cents and maintain average cost below 99 cents, exiting at break-even
Support paper trading mode with identical logic path for validation before live deployment
Log all trades, signals, risk events, and latency metrics for post-session analysis and strategy calibration
Send real-time alerts via Telegram on trade execution, risk threshold breaches, and kill switch activation
constraints: Sub-100ms end-to-end latency from Binance price update receipt to Polymarket order submission
Must handle Binance WebSocket reconnection gracefully without missing price updates during reconnect window
Polymarket CLOB API rate limits must be respected — order submission rate must stay within platform limits
Only trade contracts with >$50,000 liquidity to ensure clean entry and exit without excessive slippage
Private keys must never be hardcoded — loaded exclusively from environment variables or encrypted keystore
System must operate on Polygon network (Polymarket's L2) — USDC must be bridged to Polygon before trading

Polymarket is not available to US residents — as of the 2025 CFTC settlement, Polymarket actively monitors US wallet activity and may freeze funds of US-based users. Legal compliance with user's jurisdiction is required
The arbitrage window has compressed from 12s (2024) to ~2.7s (Q1 2026) and continues narrowing — the bot must be fast enough to operate within current and near-future windows
Must support graceful shutdown: no orphaned orders, all positions tracked, state persisted to disk
assumptions: Binance WebSocket API provides reliable sub-50ms BTC/ETH price stream via wss://stream.binance.com with miniTicker or trade streams
Polymarket CLOB API accepts programmatic order submission with two-tier auth: L1 (EIP-712) used once to derive L2 API credentials, then L2 (HMAC-SHA256) used on every request
Short-duration BTC/ETH UP/DOWN contracts (5-min and 15-min) continue to be listed on Polymarket with sufficient liquidity (>$50K per contract)
The pricing lag between CEX spot moves and Polymarket contract repricing remains >1 second, sufficient for sub-100ms bot execution
Python asyncio with aiohttp/websockets library provides sufficient performance for the latency target without requiring C/Rust components
USDC is available on Polygon network for funding the Polymarket wallet
The operator has a stable, low-latency internet connection (ideally <20ms to Binance and Polymarket API endpoints)
Kelly criterion with fractional sizing (25-50% of full Kelly) provides adequate risk-adjusted returns as demonstrated by the 0x8dxd wallet

components.name: BinancePriceFeed
components.description: Async WebSocket client that maintains a persistent connection to Binance's real-time price stream for BTC/USDT and ETH/USDT. Note: miniTicker updates at ~1000ms intervals (not 100ms). For sub-100ms detection latency, use btcusdt@aggTrade / ethusdt@aggTrade streams which emit per-trade events. Maintains a rolling price window (last 60 seconds of ticks) for momentum calculation.
responsibilities: Establish and maintain WebSocket connection to wss://stream.binance.com:9443/ws/btcusdt@miniTicker and ethusdt@miniTicker
Maintain rolling deque of (timestamp_ms, price) tuples for last 60 seconds
Calculate real-time momentum: percentage change over configurable lookback windows (30s, 60s, 120s, 300s)
Emit PriceUpdate events to the DivergenceDetector via async queue with <5ms internal latency
Handle reconnection with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, max 30s) and emit ConnectionLost/ConnectionRestored events
Track and report WebSocket message latency (time between server timestamp and local receipt)
interfaces: async start() -> None: Initialize WebSocket connection and begin streaming
async stop() -> None: Gracefully close WebSocket connection
get_current_price(symbol: str) -> PriceSnapshot: Return latest price with timestamp
get_momentum(symbol: str, window_seconds: int) -> float: Return percentage price change over window
on_price_update: AsyncQueue[PriceUpdate] — consumers read from this queue
PriceUpdate dataclass: {symbol: str, price: Decimal, timestamp_ms: int, momentum_30s: float, momentum_60s: float}

components.name: PolymarketContractScanner
components.description: Monitors active Polymarket short-duration BTC/ETH UP/DOWN contracts. Uses the Gamma API (gamma-api.polymarket.com) for contract discovery with tag/active/end_date filtering, and the CLOB API /book endpoint (or preferably WebSocket) for live orderbook data. Tracks current orderbook state (best bid/ask on both YES and NO sides) and contract metadata (expiry time, resolution oracle, current implied probability). Discovers new contracts as they open and drops expired ones.
responsibilities: Discover active BTC and ETH UP/DOWN contracts (5-min and 15-min durations) via Gamma API: GET https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/markets with tag, active, and end_date_min filtering. CLOB API /markets does not support the filtering needed for contract discovery

Subscribe to orderbook updates for tracked contracts via Polymarket WebSocket (wss://ws-subscriptions-clob.polymarket.com) as the mandatory primary data source. REST polling of CLOB API GET /book?token_id=<id> is used only for initial orderbook snapshot on contract discovery, not ongoing updates. Note: /book endpoint can return stale data under load
Calculate current implied probability from best bid/ask midpoint: p_implied = (best_bid_yes + (1 - best_ask_no)) / 2
Track contract lifecycle: opening, active, approaching_expiry (last 60s), expired, resolved
Detect new contract listings and automatically begin tracking
Assess orderbook depth and liquidity — flag contracts with <$50K total liquidity as untradeable
Emit ContractUpdate events to DivergenceDetector with current odds, spread, and liquidity metrics
interfaces: async start() -> None: Begin polling/streaming contract data
async stop() -> None: Stop all contract monitoring
get_active_contracts() -> List[ContractState]: Return all currently tradeable contracts
get_contract(condition_id: str) -> ContractState: Return specific contract state
on_contract_update: AsyncQueue[ContractUpdate] — consumers read contract state changes

ContractState dataclass: {condition_id: str, token_id_yes: str, token_id_no: str, symbol: str, duration_minutes: int, expiry_ts: int, implied_prob: float, best_bid_yes: float, best_ask_yes: float, depth_usdc: float, time_remaining_s: int}

components.name: DivergenceDetector
components.description: Core signal engine that continuously compares CEX-derived fair probability against Polymarket implied probability for each active contract. When divergence exceeds the configured threshold, emits a TradeSignal with edge magnitude, direction, and confidence score. Uses a momentum-persistence model: if BTC drops X% in the last 30-60 seconds, the probability that BTC remains below its current level at contract expiry is derived from historical momentum autocorrelation.
responsibilities: Consume PriceUpdate events from BinancePriceFeed and ContractUpdate events from PolymarketContractScanner

Staleness check: before computing divergence, verify that the ContractUpdate timestamp is within 500ms of current time. If Polymarket data is stale beyond this threshold, suppress the signal and log as stale_data_suppressed. This prevents false divergence signals caused by delayed Polymarket data rather than genuine mispricing
For each active contract, compute fair probability: p_fair = momentum_to_probability(momentum, time_remaining)
The momentum_to_probability model maps (price_change_pct, seconds_to_expiry) to a probability using a calibrated logistic function: p = 1 / (1 + exp(-k * momentum * sqrt(time_remaining / 60)))
Calculate edge: edge = abs(p_fair - p_implied). If edge > threshold (default 0.03 = 3%), emit TradeSignal
Determine direction: if p_fair > p_implied, buy YES side; if p_fair < p_implied, buy NO side
Compute confidence score based on: momentum magnitude, time remaining (more time = less certain), orderbook liquidity
Apply signal cooldown: do not re-signal the same contract within 2 seconds of a previous signal to avoid duplicate trades
Log all divergence calculations for post-session calibration of the probability model
interfaces: async start() -> None: Begin consuming price and contract feeds
async stop() -> None: Stop divergence detection
set_threshold(threshold: float) -> None: Update divergence threshold (default 0.03)
on_trade_signal: AsyncQueue[TradeSignal] — downstream consumers read signals

TradeSignal dataclass: {condition_id: str, direction: Literal['YES', 'NO'], entry_price: Decimal, fair_price: Decimal, edge: float, confidence: float, timestamp_ms: int, momentum_pct: float, time_remaining_s: int}

components.name: KellyPositionSizer
components.description: Computes optimal position size for each trade signal using fractional Kelly criterion. The full Kelly formula for a binary outcome is f* = (bp - q) / b, where b is the odds ratio (payout / risk), p is the estimated win probability, and q = 1 - p. A fractional multiplier (default 0.25 to 0.50) is applied to reduce variance. Additional hard caps enforce maximum single-position and portfolio-level exposure limits.
responsibilities: Receive TradeSignal from DivergenceDetector and current portfolio state from RiskManager
Calculate Kelly fraction: b = (1 / entry_price) - 1 (binary contract payout), p = fair_price (estimated win probability), q = 1 - p, f_full = (b*p - q) / b
Apply fractional Kelly multiplier: f_trade = f_full * kelly_fraction (configurable, default 0.25 for conservative, 0.50 for moderate)
Compute position size in USDC: size_usdc = f_trade * available_capital
Enforce hard caps: max single position = min(8% of portfolio, $5000 default), min position = $1 USDC
Adjust size for orderbook depth: if size_usdc > 50% of available depth at target price, reduce to 50% of available depth
In conservative mode (configurable), cap at 0.5% of capital per trade as documented in source 2018453276279070952
Return PositionSize with exact USDC amount, number of contracts, and effective Kelly fraction used
interfaces: compute_size(signal: TradeSignal, portfolio: PortfolioState) -> PositionSize
set_kelly_fraction(fraction: float) -> None: Update Kelly multiplier (0.0 to 1.0)
set_max_position_pct(pct: float) -> None: Update max single position as % of portfolio
PositionSize dataclass: {size_usdc: Decimal, num_contracts: int, kelly_fraction_used: float, capped: bool, cap_reason: Optional[str]}

components.name: ExecutionEngine
components.description: Handles order construction, signing, submission, and fill tracking via the Polymarket CLOB API. Uses a two-tier authentication model: L1 (EIP-712 signature from the wallet private key) is used once during initialization to derive L2 API credentials (apiKey, secret, passphrase) via the CLOB /derive-api-key endpoint. All subsequent order submissions use L2 (HMAC-SHA256) authentication with these derived credentials for lower latency. Supports limit orders at the target stale price. Tracks order lifecycle from submission through fill or cancellation.
responsibilities: Receive (TradeSignal, PositionSize) pairs from the pipeline and construct CLOB limit orders

Build order payload: actual CLOB API uses camelCase fields {tokenId, price, size, side: 'BUY', orderType: 'GTC', expiration: now_seconds + 120}. Recommend using py-clob-client OrderBuilder rather than hand-rolling payloads to avoid field name mismatches

On startup, derive L2 API credentials by signing an EIP-712 message with the wallet private key (POLYMARKET_PRIVATE_KEY) and calling POST /derive-api-key. Store the returned apiKey, secret, and passphrase in memory (or load pre-derived values from POLYMARKET_API_KEY, POLYMARKET_SECRET, POLYMARKET_PASSPHRASE env vars)
Sign all order submissions using L2 HMAC-SHA256 authentication with the derived apiKey/secret/passphrase for lower latency than per-order EIP-712 signing

Submit signed orders to Polymarket CLOB API endpoint POST /order with POLY_API_KEY, POLY_SIGNATURE, and POLY_TIMESTAMP headers and nonce management. Note: actual CLOB API uses camelCase field names (tokenId, makerAmount, takerAmount, etc.) -- recommend using py-clob-client OrderBuilder rather than hand-rolling order payloads
Track order status: PENDING -> LIVE -> MATCHED/PARTIALLY_FILLED/CANCELLED
If order is not filled within 2 seconds (stale window), cancel and log as missed opportunity
Handle API errors: rate limiting (429 -> backoff), server errors (5xx -> retry with exponential backoff max 3 attempts), invalid order (400 -> log and skip)
Maintain a local order book of all active/pending orders to prevent duplicate submissions for the same contract
Report fill events to RiskManager and TradeLogger with exact fill price, size, fees, and latency metrics
interfaces: async execute(signal: TradeSignal, size: PositionSize) -> OrderResult
async cancel_order(order_id: str) -> bool
async cancel_all() -> int: Cancel all open orders, return count cancelled
get_open_orders() -> List[Order]
on_fill: AsyncQueue[FillEvent] — downstream consumers notified of fills
OrderResult dataclass: {order_id: str, status: str, fill_price: Optional[Decimal], fill_size: Optional[Decimal], latency_ms: int, error: Optional[str]}
FillEvent dataclass: {order_id: str, condition_id: str, direction: str, fill_price: Decimal, fill_size_usdc: Decimal, fee_usdc: Decimal, timestamp_ms: int}

components.name: RiskManager
components.description: Central risk control module that enforces position-level, daily, and portfolio-level risk limits. Implements the -40% drawdown kill switch that halts all trading and flattens positions. Tracks running PnL, daily loss, open exposure, and win rate. The kill switch was the single most important differentiator between Claude (+1,322%) and OpenClaw (liquidated) in the documented head-to-head comparison.
responsibilities: Track portfolio state: starting_capital, current_capital, open_positions, realized_pnl, unrealized_pnl
Calculate running drawdown from high-water mark: drawdown_pct = (high_water_mark - current_value) / high_water_mark
Enforce kill switch: if drawdown_pct >= 0.40 (-40%), immediately cancel all open orders, prevent new order submission, emit KillSwitchActivated alert
Enforce daily loss limit: if daily_realized_loss >= daily_loss_limit (default -2% of starting capital for conservative, -20% for aggressive), halt trading until next UTC midnight
Enforce per-trade risk limit: reject any PositionSize where size_usdc > max_per_trade_pct * current_capital
Track concurrent open positions: max 5 simultaneous open positions to prevent overexposure
Monitor contract resolution: when contracts settle, update realized PnL and win/loss counters

Implement cost-averaging fallback from source 2039746395100377447: for positions in loss, allow averaging down with entries below 35 cents maintaining average cost below 99 cents, exit at break-even if arb thesis invalidated. CAVEAT: this strategy originates from a different context (UP/DOWN options with longer timeframes) and is incompatible with pure latency arbitrage where positions should be cut quickly. Treat as experimental and DISABLED by default in v1 -- enable only via explicit config flag cost_averaging_enabled: false
Emit risk alerts at threshold levels: 50% of daily limit consumed, 75% of daily limit, kill switch warning at -30%, kill switch triggered at -40%
Persist portfolio state to disk (JSON) every 60 seconds for crash recovery
interfaces: check_trade_allowed(signal: TradeSignal, size: PositionSize) -> RiskDecision
record_fill(fill: FillEvent) -> None
record_settlement(condition_id: str, payout: Decimal) -> None
get_portfolio_state() -> PortfolioState
is_killed() -> bool: Check if kill switch is active
reset_daily_limits() -> None: Called at UTC midnight
RiskDecision dataclass: {allowed: bool, reason: Optional[str], adjusted_size: Optional[PositionSize]}
PortfolioState dataclass: {capital: Decimal, high_water_mark: Decimal, drawdown_pct: float, daily_pnl: Decimal, open_positions: int, total_trades: int, win_rate: float, is_killed: bool}

components.name: AlertService
components.description: Sends real-time notifications via Telegram Bot API for trade executions, risk threshold breaches, kill switch activation, connection issues, and daily summary reports.
responsibilities: Send Telegram messages via Bot API (POST https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/sendMessage)
Alert on: trade fills, daily PnL summary, risk threshold breaches (50%/75% daily limit), kill switch activation, WebSocket disconnection/reconnection, errors
Rate-limit outgoing messages to avoid Telegram API throttling (max 30 messages/minute)
Format messages with key metrics: trade direction, size, price, edge, running PnL, win rate
Queue alerts asynchronously so alerting never blocks the trading pipeline
interfaces: async send_alert(level: Literal['INFO', 'WARNING', 'CRITICAL'], message: str) -> None
async send_trade_alert(fill: FillEvent, portfolio: PortfolioState) -> None
async send_daily_summary(portfolio: PortfolioState) -> None
configure(bot_token: str, chat_id: str) -> None

components.name: TradeLogger
components.description: Structured logging system that records all signals, trades, risk events, and performance metrics to both file (JSON lines) and in-memory data structures for real-time dashboard queries.
responsibilities: Log every TradeSignal with full context: timestamp, divergence, momentum, contract state, edge, confidence
Log every OrderResult with latency breakdown: signal_to_order_ms, order_to_fill_ms, total_latency_ms
Log every RiskDecision including rejections with reasons
Log every settlement with pnl attribution
Maintain rolling performance metrics: 1h/4h/24h win rate, avg edge, avg latency, sharpe ratio
Write to rotating log files: trades.jsonl, signals.jsonl, risk.jsonl, performance.jsonl
Support CSV export for backtesting and analysis
interfaces: log_signal(signal: TradeSignal) -> None
log_order(result: OrderResult) -> None
log_risk_event(decision: RiskDecision) -> None
log_settlement(condition_id: str, pnl: Decimal) -> None
get_performance(window_hours: int) -> PerformanceMetrics
export_csv(filepath: str, start_date: str, end_date: str) -> None

components.name: BotOrchestrator
components.description: Top-level coordinator that initializes all components, manages the async event loop, wires together the pipeline (PriceFeed -> DivergenceDetector -> KellySizer -> ExecutionEngine), handles graceful startup/shutdown, and manages the paper-trading mode toggle.
responsibilities: Load configuration from config.yaml and environment variables
Initialize all components in dependency order: AlertService, TradeLogger, RiskManager, BinancePriceFeed, PolymarketContractScanner, DivergenceDetector, KellyPositionSizer, ExecutionEngine

Wire the async pipeline: PriceFeed.on_price_update -> DivergenceDetector, ContractScanner.on_contract_update -> DivergenceDetector, DivergenceDetector.on_trade_signal -> pipeline(KellySizer -> RiskManager.check -> ExecutionEngine)
Support paper mode: when enabled, ExecutionEngine simulates fills at current market price without submitting real orders
Handle SIGINT/SIGTERM: cancel all open orders, persist state, close WebSocket connections, log final summary
Schedule daily tasks: reset daily risk limits at UTC midnight, send daily summary alert
Monitor component health: restart WebSocket connections if heartbeat missed for >30 seconds
interfaces: async run(mode: Literal['paper', 'live']) -> None: Main entry point
async shutdown() -> None: Graceful shutdown sequence
get_status() -> BotStatus: Return current operational status of all components

BotStatus dataclass: {mode: Literal['paper', 'live'], uptime_seconds: int, binance_connected: bool, polymarket_connected: bool, divergence_detector_active: bool, risk_manager_killed: bool, open_orders: int, open_positions: int, total_trades: int, win_rate: float, daily_pnl: Decimal, drawdown_pct: float, last_signal_ts: Optional[int], last_fill_ts: Optional[int]}

architecture.data_flow: 1. BinancePriceFeed receives real-time BTC/ETH price via WebSocket. For sub-100ms detection, use btcusdt@aggTrade / ethusdt@aggTrade streams (per-trade events), not miniTicker which only updates at ~1000ms intervals. Feed calculates rolling momentum (30s/60s/300s % change) and pushes PriceUpdate to async queue. 2. PolymarketContractScanner discovers active contracts via Gamma API (GET https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/markets with tag/active/end_date filtering) and fetches initial orderbook snapshot from CLOB API (GET /book?token_id=<id>). Ongoing orderbook updates are received via mandatory WebSocket connection (wss://ws-subscriptions-clob.polymarket.com), subscribing to book channel per token_id. REST /book polling is fallback only. Pushes ContractUpdate to async queue. Divergence is only computed when ContractUpdate timestamp is within 500ms of current time; stale data is suppressed. 3. DivergenceDetector consumes both queues. On each PriceUpdate, it iterates all active contracts and recalculates: p_fair = momentum_to_probability(momentum_30s, time_remaining_s) using calibrated logistic model. Computes edge = |p_fair - p_implied|. If edge > threshold (default 3%), creates TradeSignal with direction (YES if p_fair > p_implied, NO otherwise), entry_price (current best ask on target side), and edge magnitude. 4. TradeSignal passes to KellyPositionSizer which calculates: b = (1/entry_price) - 1, f* = (b*p_fair - (1-p_fair)) / b, size = f* * kelly_fraction * available_capital, capped at min(8% portfolio, available_depth * 0.5). 5. RiskManager.check_trade_allowed validates: not killed, daily loss not exceeded, position count < max, size within per-trade limit. Returns RiskDecision. 6. If allowed, ExecutionEngine constructs order using py-clob-client OrderBuilder (camelCase fields), signs with L2 HMAC-SHA256 (derived from initial EIP-712 L1 auth), submits to Polymarket CLOB POST /order. Expiration set to now + 120 seconds (Polymarket requires >= now + 60s). Tracks fill with 2-second timeout. 7. FillEvent flows back to RiskManager (update portfolio state), TradeLogger (record trade), and AlertService (send Telegram notification). 8. On contract resolution, settlement data flows to RiskManager for realized PnL update and win/loss tracking. Full pipeline target: <100ms from PriceUpdate receipt to order submission.
integration_points: Binance WebSocket API: wss://stream.binance.com:9443/ws/<symbol>@miniTicker — real-time price streaming, no authentication required for public streams, rate limit: 5 messages/second outbound, handles ping/pong keepalive every 3 minutes

Polymarket Gamma API: https://gamma-api.polymarket.com — REST endpoints for /markets with tag, active, and end_date_min filtering. Used for contract discovery (finding active BTC/ETH UP/DOWN markets). No authentication required. This is separate from the CLOB API and provides richer market metadata

Polymarket CLOB API: https://clob.polymarket.com — REST endpoints for /book, /order, /cancel. Two-tier authentication: L1 (EIP-712 wallet signature) used once to derive L2 credentials via POST /derive-api-key, then L2 (HMAC-SHA256 with apiKey/secret/passphrase) used on every subsequent request. Rate limit: approximately 10 requests/second. Order format uses camelCase fields (tokenId, makerAmount, takerAmount) -- use py-clob-client OrderBuilder

Polymarket WebSocket: wss://ws-subscriptions-clob.polymarket.com — mandatory primary source for live orderbook updates. Subscribe to price_change and book channels per token_id. Lower latency and more reliable than REST polling of /book endpoint
Polygon Network (Matic): JSON-RPC endpoint for on-chain transaction submission if needed for contract settlement monitoring. Use wss://polygon-rpc.com or Alchemy/Infura endpoint
Telegram Bot API: https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/sendMessage — for real-time alerts. Requires bot token (from @BotFather) and chat_id. Rate limit: 30 messages/minute per chat

System filesystem: config.yaml for bot configuration, .env for secrets (POLYMARKET_PRIVATE_KEY, POLYMARKET_API_KEY, POLYMARKET_SECRET, POLYMARKET_PASSPHRASE, BINANCE_API_KEY, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID), JSON files for state persistence and trade logs

phases.name: Phase 1: Core Infrastructure and Price Feed
phases.description: Establish the async foundation, configuration system, and Binance WebSocket price feed. This phase produces a running process that connects to Binance, streams live BTC/ETH prices, calculates rolling momentum, and logs all data — validating the critical sub-50ms latency requirement before building downstream components.
tasks: Set up Python project structure: pyproject.toml with dependencies (websockets, aiohttp, python-dotenv, pydantic), src/ package layout, config.yaml schema

Implement config loader: read config.yaml for strategy params (threshold, kelly_fraction, risk_limits, momentum_model.k_btc, momentum_model.k_eth) and .env for secrets. The momentum model k values control the logistic sensitivity per asset and must be configurable for calibration

Implement BinancePriceFeed: async WebSocket client using websockets library, connect to wss://stream.binance.com:9443/ws/btcusdt@miniTicker, parse miniTicker JSON, maintain rolling deque of (timestamp_ms, price) for last 60 seconds
Implement momentum calculator: compute 30s, 60s, 120s, 300s percentage changes from rolling price window
Implement WebSocket reconnection: exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, max 30s), connection health monitoring via ping/pong
Implement TradeLogger foundation: structured JSON lines logging to rotating files with configurable rotation size
Implement BotOrchestrator skeleton: asyncio.run() entry point, signal handlers for SIGINT/SIGTERM, component lifecycle management
Write latency benchmark: measure and log time from Binance server timestamp to local PriceUpdate emission, verify <50ms
deliverables: Running async process that streams BTC/ETH prices from Binance WebSocket
Verified sub-50ms message receipt latency with logged benchmarks
Rolling momentum calculations validated against manual computation
Automatic reconnection verified by simulating connection drops
Structured log output in trades.jsonl format

phases.name: Phase 2: Polymarket Integration and Divergence Detection
phases.description: Add Polymarket CLOB API integration for contract discovery and orderbook monitoring. Implement the divergence detection engine with the momentum-to-probability model. This phase produces trade signals without executing them — pure signal generation for validation.
tasks: Implement PolymarketContractScanner: discover active crypto UP/DOWN contracts via Gamma API (GET https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/markets with tag/active/end_date filtering), parse response for condition_id, token_ids, expiry, category. Do not use CLOB API /markets for discovery

Implement orderbook fetcher: initial snapshot via GET /book?token_id=<id> from CLOB API, then subscribe to wss://ws-subscriptions-clob.polymarket.com book channel for live updates (mandatory). Parse bids/asks, compute best bid/ask and implied probability. Note: /book REST endpoint can return stale data under load -- use WebSocket as primary source
Implement contract lifecycle tracking: detect new contracts, track time_remaining_s, flag contracts approaching expiry (<60s remaining)
Implement liquidity filter: compute total depth in USDC from orderbook, reject contracts with depth < $50,000
Implement DivergenceDetector: consume PriceUpdate and ContractUpdate queues, compute p_fair using logistic momentum model
Calibrate momentum_to_probability model: p = 1 / (1 + exp(-k * momentum_pct * sqrt(time_remaining / 60))), initial k=15 based on BTC 15-min autocorrelation
Implement signal cooldown: suppress duplicate signals for same contract within 2-second window
Implement signal logging: log every divergence calculation (both above and below threshold) for model calibration
Add paper mode signal tracking: record hypothetical entry and compare against resolution to compute theoretical win rate
deliverables: Live contract scanning showing active BTC/ETH UP/DOWN markets with implied probabilities
Divergence detection generating TradeSignal events when edge > threshold
Signal accuracy validated against contract resolutions in paper mode (target: >70% win rate over 200+ signals)
Model calibration data: logged divergence vs. actual resolution outcomes

phases.name: Phase 3: Position Sizing and Risk Management
phases.description: Implement the fractional Kelly position sizer and the full risk management suite including the -40% kill switch. This is the most critical phase — the Claude vs OpenClaw experiment proved that risk management quality is the primary determinant of survival and profitability.
tasks: Implement KellyPositionSizer: full Kelly formula f* = (bp - q) / b for binary contracts, apply fractional multiplier (default 0.25)
Implement position cap logic: min(kelly_size, 8% of portfolio, 50% of orderbook depth, max_position_usdc)
Implement conservative mode: 0.5% capital per trade cap as documented in winkle's build guide
Implement RiskManager: track portfolio state (capital, high_water_mark, drawdown, daily_pnl, open_positions, win_rate)
Implement kill switch: if (high_water_mark - current_value) / high_water_mark >= 0.40, set is_killed = true, emit KillSwitchActivated
Implement daily loss limit: track daily_realized_loss, halt trading when >= daily_loss_limit_pct of starting capital
Implement concurrent position limit: max 5 simultaneous open positions

Implement cost-averaging fallback (EXPERIMENTAL, disabled by default in v1 via cost_averaging_enabled: false): for positions in loss, allow additional entries below 35 cents, track weighted average cost, exit at break-even if average cost < 99 cents. This originates from a different strategy context (UP/DOWN options) and is incompatible with pure latency arbitrage
Implement state persistence: write PortfolioState to portfolio_state.json every 60 seconds, load on startup for crash recovery
Implement daily limit reset: schedule reset_daily_limits() at UTC midnight via asyncio
Write risk unit tests: verify kill switch triggers at exactly -40%, daily limit halts trading, position caps enforced
deliverables: Kelly position sizer computing correct sizes for various edge/probability scenarios
Kill switch verified to activate at -40% drawdown and prevent all further trading
Daily loss limit verified to halt trading at configured threshold
State persistence verified: crash and restart recovers portfolio state accurately
Unit test suite passing for all risk scenarios

phases.name: Phase 4: Execution Engine and Paper Trading Validation
phases.description: Build the order execution pipeline with EIP-712 signature support and Polymarket CLOB submission. Run the complete system in paper mode for at least one week (200+ trades) to validate end-to-end performance before live deployment.
tasks: Implement ExecutionEngine: construct CLOB order payload using py-clob-client OrderBuilder with camelCase fields {tokenId, price, size, side, orderType, expiration: now_seconds + 120}. Polymarket requires expiration >= now + 60 seconds; use a configurable short window (default 120s) rather than contract_expiry_ts
Implement EIP-712 order signing: build typed data structure per Polymarket CLOB spec, sign with eth_account library using private key from env var
Implement order submission: POST to CLOB API /order endpoint with signed payload, parse response for order_id and status
Implement order lifecycle tracking: poll order status (PENDING -> LIVE -> MATCHED), timeout and cancel after 2 seconds if unfilled
Implement fill detection and reporting: emit FillEvent with exact fill price, size, fees, and full latency breakdown
Implement cancel_all(): iterate open orders and cancel each, used by kill switch and graceful shutdown
Implement paper mode in ExecutionEngine: simulate fills at current best ask without submitting real orders, use same code path for all downstream logic
Wire complete pipeline in BotOrchestrator: PriceFeed -> DivergenceDetector -> KellySizer -> RiskCheck -> ExecutionEngine -> RiskUpdate + AlertService
Implement AlertService: Telegram Bot API integration for trade fills, risk alerts, and daily summaries
Run paper trading validation: operate for minimum 7 days, collect 200+ completed trades, compute win rate, average edge, average latency, max drawdown
Document paper trading results and compare against 0x8dxd benchmarks (target: >70% win rate, sub-100ms latency)
deliverables: Complete end-to-end pipeline running in paper mode
Order signing and submission verified against Polymarket CLOB API (can verify with a $1 live test order)
Paper trading results: 200+ trades with documented win rate, edge, and latency metrics
Telegram alerts working for all event types
Sub-100ms pipeline latency verified from price update to order construction

phases.name: Phase 5: Live Deployment, Monitoring, and Scaling
phases.description: Transition from paper to live trading with graduated position sizes. Establish monitoring, operational procedures, and scaling guidelines. Start with $1-5 per trade and scale only on evidence of live/paper convergence.
tasks: Implement live/paper mode switch in config.yaml with explicit confirmation required for live mode
Deploy with minimal position sizes: start at $1-5 USDC per trade regardless of Kelly recommendation
Monitor first 50 live trades: compare fill prices, win rate, and latency against paper mode baselines
Implement performance dashboard: real-time CLI display showing current positions, PnL, win rate, latency, drawdown, kill switch status
Implement graduated scaling protocol: if live win rate within 5% of paper win rate after 50 trades, double position size; repeat weekly
Configure systemd/pm2 process management for unattended operation with auto-restart on crash
Implement health check endpoint: HTTP server on localhost exposing /health with component status for external monitoring
Document operational runbook: daily checks, configuration changes, emergency procedures, kill switch manual override
Implement edge compression monitoring: track average divergence window duration over time, alert when average drops below 1.5 seconds
Plan strategy evolution: when latency arb edge compresses below profitability threshold, evaluate oracle arb or market making as next strategies
deliverables: Live bot running with real capital at graduated position sizes
Live vs paper performance comparison documented
Process management configured for 24/7 unattended operation
Operational runbook covering all procedures
Edge compression monitoring active with alerts
Scaling plan with evidence-based position size progression

tech_stack: Python 3.11+: Core language — async/await native support, strong ecosystem for crypto/trading
asyncio: Event loop and coroutine management for concurrent WebSocket streams and order execution
websockets: Async WebSocket client library for Binance price feed connection
aiohttp: Async HTTP client for Polymarket CLOB REST API calls and Telegram Bot API
pydantic: Data validation and settings management for configuration and message types

py-clob-client: Official Polymarket CLOB client library — provides OrderBuilder for correct order payload construction (camelCase fields), L1/L2 auth helpers, and API wrappers. Strongly recommended over hand-rolling API calls
eth-account: Ethereum account management and EIP-712 typed data signing for Polymarket L1 auth (used once to derive L2 credentials)
web3.py: Polygon network interaction for on-chain monitoring if needed
python-dotenv: Environment variable loading for secrets management
PyYAML: Configuration file parsing for config.yaml
structlog: Structured logging with JSON output for trade and signal logs
pytest + pytest-asyncio: Test framework for async unit and integration tests
USDC on Polygon: Trading capital denomination — must be bridged to Polygon network before use

risks.description: Edge compression: The arbitrage window has shrunk from 12+ seconds (2024) to ~2.7 seconds (Q1 2026). As more bots enter the space, the window will continue narrowing. Below ~0.5 seconds, the strategy becomes uneconomical for non-co-located infrastructure, potentially making the entire bot worthless.
risks.mitigation: Monitor average divergence window duration continuously. Alert when window drops below 1.5 seconds. Treat the operation as time-limited — extract value while edge exists. Plan migration to alternative strategies (oracle arb, market making) before window closes. Track competitor bot count via Polymarket API fill patterns.

risks.description: Kill switch failure: A bug in the -40% drawdown kill switch — the single most important risk control — could allow the bot to continue trading through catastrophic losses. The OpenClaw liquidation proved that absent proper kill switch logic, even high-win-rate strategies can blow up the entire portfolio.
risks.mitigation: Unit test kill switch exhaustively: test at exactly -39.9% (should not trigger), -40.0% (should trigger), -40.1% (should trigger). Test with rapid sequential losses. Test state persistence — kill switch must remain active after restart. Implement secondary watchdog process that independently monitors portfolio value and kills the main process if drawdown exceeds threshold.

risks.description: Polymarket API/rules changes: Polymarket can modify contract mechanics, settlement rules, CLOB API endpoints, or rate limits at any time without notice. A contract pricing change or API deprecation could invalidate the strategy overnight.
risks.mitigation: Monitor Polymarket changelog, Discord, and developer documentation. Implement API response validation — if response schema changes unexpectedly, halt trading and alert. Pin to known API version. Maintain manual override capability to halt bot remotely via Telegram command.

risks.description: WebSocket disconnection during active positions: If the Binance WebSocket connection drops while positions are open, the bot loses its price signal and cannot detect when to exit or avoid new entries based on stale data.
risks.mitigation: Implement heartbeat monitoring with 3-second timeout. On disconnection: immediately halt new order submission, keep existing positions (they are directional bets that will resolve), attempt reconnection with exponential backoff. Log gap duration. If gap exceeds 30 seconds, alert via Telegram. Never trade on stale price data — require price update within last 2 seconds for any new signal.

risks.description: Position sizing bug: A miscalculation in Kelly sizing or failure to enforce caps could result in a single position consuming 80%+ of the portfolio. One losing trade at that size would be catastrophic. This is more dangerous than a bad strategy.
risks.mitigation: Implement layered caps: Kelly fraction (25-50%), hard max % of portfolio (8%), hard max USD ($5000), orderbook depth limit (50% of available). Each cap is independent — the lowest one wins. Unit test each cap independently. Log the cap that bound on every trade for monitoring. Add assertion that no order exceeds 8% of current capital — crash the bot if assertion fails rather than submit the order.

risks.description: Private key compromise: The Polymarket wallet private key is required for order signing. If leaked (hardcoded in source, committed to git, logged to file), an attacker can drain the entire wallet immediately.
risks.mitigation: Load private key exclusively from environment variable (POLYMARKET_PRIVATE_KEY). Never log, print, or include in error messages. Add .env to .gitignore. Use a dedicated wallet with only trading capital — do not use a wallet containing other assets. Consider hardware wallet integration for large balances.

risks.description: Latency exceeding target: If the full pipeline (price update -> divergence detection -> Kelly sizing -> order construction -> API submission) exceeds 100ms, the bot will consistently miss the arbitrage window, resulting in fills at already-corrected prices with no edge.
risks.mitigation: Benchmark each pipeline stage independently. Optimize hot path: pre-compute Kelly parameters, cache contract metadata, use connection pooling for HTTP requests. If Python performance is insufficient, consider porting the hot path (divergence detection + order construction) to Cython or a Rust extension. Use a VPS geographically close to both Binance and Polymarket API servers.

risks.description: Model miscalibration: The momentum_to_probability logistic model parameter (k) may be incorrectly calibrated, producing systematically wrong fair probability estimates. This would generate false signals (low edge where none exists) or miss real signals (high edge not detected).
risks.mitigation: Log all divergence calculations including sub-threshold ones. After 500+ contract resolutions in paper mode, regress actual outcomes against predicted probabilities to recalibrate k. Use paper mode win rate as the primary calibration metric — if win rate is below 70% after 200 trades, recalibrate before going live.

risks.description: Insufficient orderbook liquidity: If the target contract has thin orderbook depth, the bot's order may move the market (market impact), fill at a worse price than expected, or not fill at all within the 2-second window.
risks.mitigation: Filter contracts by minimum liquidity ($50K total depth). Size positions to no more than 50% of available depth at target price. Use limit orders (not market orders) to avoid adverse fills. Track fill rate and slippage metrics — if fill rate drops below 70%, investigate and potentially lower position sizes or widen the divergence threshold.

risks.description: Regulatory risk: Polymarket is not available to US residents. Following the 2025 CFTC settlement, Polymarket actively monitors US wallet activity and may freeze funds. Jurisdictional regulations around prediction market trading, automated trading, and crypto derivatives vary and can change. Operating in violation could result in legal consequences and frozen funds.
risks.mitigation: Verify legal status in operator's jurisdiction before deployment. Do not use VPNs to circumvent geo-restrictions — Polymarket actively detects and enforces geo-restrictions post-CFTC settlement. Consult legal counsel for large-scale operations. Maintain withdrawal readiness — do not keep more capital on Polymarket than necessary for active trading.

success_criteria: Paper mode win rate exceeds 70% over a minimum of 200 completed trades within the first 7 days of operation
End-to-end pipeline latency (Binance price update receipt to Polymarket order submission) consistently under 100ms, measured and logged per trade
Binance WebSocket connection maintains >99.5% uptime with automatic reconnection completing within 5 seconds
Kill switch activates within 1 second of portfolio drawdown reaching -40% from high-water mark, verified by unit tests and live monitoring
Daily loss limit halts trading within 1 trade of the configured threshold (default -2% conservative / -20% aggressive)
No single position exceeds 8% of total portfolio value, enforced by layered caps with logged cap reasons
Live trading win rate converges within 5 percentage points of paper mode win rate after 50 live trades
Zero instances of private key exposure in logs, error messages, or version control
Telegram alerts delivered within 5 seconds for all trade fills, risk threshold breaches, and kill switch activations
Bot runs unattended for 72+ hours without manual intervention (excluding planned maintenance), with automatic recovery from WebSocket disconnections and transient API errors
Average net profit per trade (after transaction fees, gas costs, and slippage) exceeds $0.50 USDC minimum, with aggregate daily profit exceeding $50 USDC to justify operational overhead
State persistence enables crash recovery: after simulated kill and restart, portfolio state matches pre-crash values within $1 USDC
notes: This spec synthesizes 6 research sources documenting the 0x8dxd Polymarket arbitrage bot ($313 to $2.38M, 26,738 trades, 98% win rate) and related implementations. Key insight from the Claude vs OpenClaw comparison: risk management (fractional Kelly + kill switch) was the decisive factor, not strategy sophistication. The arbitrage edge is real but time-limited — the window has compressed from 12s to 2.7s and continues narrowing. Implementation priority should be: (1) reliable price feed, (2) bulletproof risk management, (3) execution speed. The cost-averaging fallback from source 2039746395100377447 provides a complementary exit mechanism for positions where the primary arb thesis fails. Conservative risk parameters (0.5% per trade, 2% daily loss) from source 2018453276279070952 should be the default for initial deployment, scaling to more aggressive parameters only after live validation.
